_readme: Researched enrichment, laid over the crawl. data/canonical/*.json is rewritten
wholesale by importers/import_overpass.py, so anything typed into it is lost on
the next crawl. Facts we go and find ourselves live here instead, keyed by place
id, and are merged at build time by enrich() in build.py.
Precedence, weakest to strongest: OSM crawl -> this file -> owner claim.
The owner is always the last word on their own number.
Every field carries its own provenance: src (the URL we read
it off), license, and fetched (ISO date). Only first-hand sources belong here —
the place's own site, its own LINE OA, an official register. Not a directory
site's copy of it, and not a directory's listing card for it — Google Maps' or
Facebook's rendering of a place is the directory's copy, not the place's word.
A page the place ITSELF writes and runs IS its own site, whatever it is hosted
on. In this city that is usually a Facebook page: the 2026-08-16 own-site pass
found 341 of 747 websites dead, and a business with no website still posts its
hours daily to Facebook. Reading that page is first-hand and belongs here.
(The earlier wording banned 'a scrape of Google or Facebook listings' flatly.
That entered in 8f2a6acc4c beside enrich_sites.py and names no decider; Nan,
2026-09-06: not her rule — 'I don't clutch pearls about scraping.' What
survives is the directory/own-page line above, which is about who authored
the fact, not about which company hosts it.)
Shape:
"<place id>": {
"src": "https://…", "license": "official-site", "fetched": "2026-08-16",
"note": "optional, why this was hard or what is still missing"
Per-field overrides go in "prov": {"<field>": {"src":…, "fetched":…}}.
